title.ko: 도치 조건문: Had I known · Were he to · Should you need
title.en: inverted conditionals: Had I known, Were he to, Should you need

explain.ko: 도치 조건문은 if를 생략하고 조동사를 주어 앞으로 보내 격식 있는 조건절을 만드는 방법입니다. 과거 가정은 Had + 주어 + 과거분사, 가능성이 낮은 미래나 현재 가정은 Were + 주어 + to + 동사원형 또는 Were + 주어, 가능성이 있는 미래 상황은 Should + 주어 + 동사원형을 씁니다. 부정은 not을 주어 뒤에 둡니다(Had it not been for ...). 공식 안내문, 계약서, 연설에서 자주 보입니다.
explain.en: Inverted conditionals drop if and move the auxiliary before the subject to form a formal condition. Use Had + subject + past participle for past hypotheses, Were + subject + to-infinitive (or Were + subject) for unlikely present or future hypotheses, and Should + subject + base verb for possible future situations. The negative puts not after the subject (Had it not been for ...). They are common in notices, contracts and speeches.

head: 유형 / Type
형태 / Form

rows: Had + S + p.p., S would have p.p.
Had I known, I would have called.

Were + S + to + base, S would
Were he to leave, we would struggle.
Had it not been for her, we'd have failed.

notes.ko: Had와 Were는 if 없이 쓰며, Should는 정중한 공식 요청에 자주 쓰입니다.
notes.en: Had and Were replace if; should is common in polite, formal requests.

notes.ko: 부정은 Hadn't I known가 아니라 Had I not known입니다.
notes.en: The negative is Had I not known, not Hadn't I known.

notes.ko: 일상 대화에서는 일반적인 if절이 더 자연스럽습니다.
notes.en: In everyday speech, ordinary if clauses sound more natural.

task.model: Had I known, I would have prepared more thoroughly. Should the schedule change, we will let you know immediately. Should you need support, please contact us at any time. Were that to happen again, we would respond in a different way.

model_trans.ko: 미리 알았더라면 더 철저히 준비했을 것입니다. 일정이 바뀐다면 즉시 알려 드리겠습니다. 지원이 필요하시면 언제든지 연락 주세요. 그런 일이 다시 일어난다면 우리는 다른 방식으로 대응할 것입니다.
model_trans.en: Had I known, I would have prepared more thoroughly. Should the schedule change, we will let you know immediately. Should you need support, please contact us at any time. Were that to happen again, we would respond in a different way.
